lines.text: This question gives you three side lengths. You only need one of them.

lines.text: Hiding in the picture is a special triangle. Once you spot it, the answer pops right out.

lines.text: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's go triangle hunting.
lines.caption: Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's go triangle hunting.

lines.text: Here's the question.
lines.caption: Here's the question.

lines.text: Triangle A B C has A B and A C both equal to ten, and B C equal to twelve.
lines.caption: Triangle A B C has A B and A C both equal to ten, and B C equal to twelve.

lines.text: A line through point A runs parallel to B C.
lines.caption: A line through point A runs parallel to B C.

lines.text: The line that cuts angle A B C exactly in half meets this line at point F.
lines.caption: The line that cuts angle A B C exactly in half meets this line at point F.

lines.text: How long is A F?
lines.caption: How long is A F?

lines.text: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.
lines.caption: Here are the five choices. Take a good look.

lines.text: So what do we know? The top line and B C never meet. They're parallel.
lines.caption: So what do we know? The top line and B C never meet. They're parallel.

lines.text: The line from B to F splits the corner at B into two equal angles. That's what bisector means.
lines.caption: The line from B to F splits the corner at B into two equal angles. That's what bisector means.

lines.text: We want the length of A F, the piece of the top line from A to F.
lines.caption: We want the length of A F, the piece of the top line from A to F.

lines.text: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!
lines.caption: Now it's your turn. Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

lines.text: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: chase the angles.
lines.caption: Welcome back! Here's the strategy: chase the angles.

lines.text: The bisector splits angle B into two equal parts. Let's call each part x.
lines.caption: The bisector splits angle B into two equal parts. Let's call each part x.

lines.text: Now look for a Z shape. The line B F crosses the two parallel lines.
lines.caption: Now look for a Z shape. The line B F crosses the two parallel lines.

lines.text: Inside a Z, the two corner angles are equal. So the angle at F is also x!
lines.caption: Inside a Z, the two corner angles are equal. So the angle at F is also x!

lines.text: Now look at triangle A B F. It has two equal angles, both x.
lines.caption: Now look at triangle A B F. It has two equal angles, both x.

lines.text: A triangle with two equal angles has two equal sides, the sides opposite those angles.
lines.caption: A triangle with two equal angles has two equal sides, the sides opposite those angles.

lines.text: Side A F sits across from the angle at B. Side A B sits across from the angle at F. So A F equals A B.
lines.caption: Side A F sits across from the angle at B. Side A B sits across from the angle at F. So A F equals A B.

lines.text: A B is ten, so A F is ten. That's Choice D!
lines.caption: A B is ten, so A F is ten. That's Choice D!

lines.text: Here's another way to see it. Let's build a shape.
lines.caption: Here's another way to see it. Let's build a shape.

lines.text: Mark a point G on B C so that B G is ten, the same as A B.
lines.caption: Mark a point G on B C so that B G is ten, the same as A B.

lines.text: Now mark the spot ten along the top line from A. Let's check that the bisector lands exactly there.
lines.caption: Now mark the spot ten along the top line from A. Let's check that the bisector lands exactly there.

lines.text: Join it up with A, B and G. The top and bottom are parallel and both ten.
lines.caption: Join it up with A, B and G. The top and bottom are parallel and both ten.

lines.text: Parallel and equal top and bottom make a parallelogram, so the slanted sides match too.
lines.caption: Parallel and equal top and bottom make a parallelogram, so the slanted sides match too.

lines.text: That's ten and ten. All four sides are ten. A rhombus!
lines.caption: That's ten and ten. All four sides are ten. A rhombus!

lines.text: A rhombus's diagonal cuts its corner exactly in half.
lines.caption: A rhombus's diagonal cuts its corner exactly in half.

lines.text: So the bisector from B goes right through that spot. It's F, ten from A. Same answer!
lines.caption: So the bisector from B goes right through that spot. It's F, ten from A. Same answer!

lines.text: When would you pick this way? When you'd rather build a shape than chase angles. Both work!
lines.caption: When would you pick this way? When you'd rather build a shape than chase angles. Both work!

lines.text: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.
lines.caption: Now let's look at the wrong answers. Each one is a trap.

lines.text: Choice B, six, is half of B C. That's a real length in the picture, but not A F.
lines.caption: Choice B, six, is half of B C. That's a real length in the picture, but not A F.

lines.text: Choice E, twelve, is B C itself. A F is parallel to B C, but it isn't the same length.
lines.caption: Choice E, twelve, is B C itself. A F is parallel to B C, but it isn't the same length.

lines.text: Choice C, eight, is the height of the triangle, from A straight down to B C. That's a real length, but the wrong one.
lines.caption: Choice C, eight, is the height of the triangle, from A straight down to B C. That's a real length, but the wrong one.

lines.text: Choice A, five, is what you'd get if you cut A B in half.
lines.caption: Choice A, five, is what you'd get if you cut A B in half.

lines.text: So here's a great habit. When you see a bisector and a parallel line, look for an isosceles triangle.
lines.caption: So here's a great habit. When you see a bisector and a parallel line, look for an isosceles triangle.

lines.text: A B is seven, A C is nine, and B C is ten.
lines.caption: A B is seven, A C is nine, and B C is ten.

lines.text: Again, a line through A runs parallel to B C, and the bisector of angle B meets it at F.
lines.caption: Again, a line through A runs parallel to B C, and the bisector of angle B meets it at F.

lines.text: The Z shape across the parallel lines makes the angle at F equal x too.

lines.text: So triangle A B F has two equal angles, and A F equals A B.
lines.caption: So triangle A B F has two equal angles, and A F equals A B.

lines.text: So the length of A F is seven!
lines.caption: So the length of A F is seven!

lines.text: Here's the sneaky part. The nine and the ten didn't matter at all. If you got seven, well done!
lines.caption: Here's the sneaky part. The nine and the ten didn't matter at all. If you got seven, well done!

lines.text: Here's the big idea to remember.
lines.caption: Here's the big idea to remember.

lines.text: A parallel line makes Z angles equal.
lines.caption: A parallel line makes Z angles equal.

lines.text: So when a bisector crosses a parallel line, look for a triangle with two equal angles. Two of its sides match!
lines.caption: So when a bisector crosses a parallel line, look for a triangle with two equal angles. Two of its sides match!
